Tu joues contre les pions pendants: You play against the hanging pawns
Deux pions côte à côte en c4 et d4, sans: Two pawns side by side on c4 and d4, with no neighbouring pawn on the b- or e-file, on two half-open files for your opponent. Strong as long as they stay side by side and plenty of pieces remain, weak if they are forced to advance or in the endgame.
Garde-les côte à côte : ensemble, ils ti: Keep them side by side: together they control b5, c5, d5 and e5 and give you space.
Tours derrière eux (Tc1, Td1), dame en e: Rooks behind them (Rc1, Rd1), queen on e2 or b3, light-squared bishop aimed at the enemy king.
Prépare la poussée d4-d5 (ou c4-c5) pour: Prepare the d4-d5 (or c4-c5) push for the moment it opens lines towards the king or frees your pieces: not before, or it hands your opponent a square.
Évite les échanges de pièces : en finale: Avoid piece trades: in the endgame, the two pawns become targets.
Ton but : les forcer à avancer. Un pion: Your goal: force them to advance. A pawn that moves leaves a square behind it for your pieces (c5 or d5) and becomes isolated or blockaded.
Pression frontale : tours en c8 et d8, f: Frontal pressure: rooks on c8 and d8, bishop on b7 or f6 aiming at d4, a knight hitting c4 (from a5 or e5).
Attaque-les par les côtés avec …b5 ou …e: Attack them from the side with …b5 or …e5 when you can.
Échange des pièces : chaque échange rapp: Trade pieces: every trade brings the endgame closer, where hanging pawns are weak.
Tu joues contre le pion isolé: You play against the isolated pawn
Un pion en d4 sans pion voisin en c ni e: A pawn on d4 with no neighbouring pawn on the c- or e-file. It gives you space and squares (e5, c5) for your pieces, but no pawn can ever defend it: in the endgame it's a weakness. The fight is “activity versus structure”.
Joue pour l'activité et l'attaque, tant: Play for activity and attack while the pieces are on: knight on e5 (the typical plan), bishop on d3 or b1 and queen on c2 or d3 aiming at h7.
Tour en e1, parfois levée de tour Te3-g3: Rook on e1, sometimes a rook lift Re3-g3 or h3 towards the king.
La poussée d4-d5 au bon moment ouvre le: The d4-d5 push at the right moment opens the game and swaps your weak pawn for activity: prepare it (Rd1, centralised pieces).
Évite les échanges, surtout de pièces mi: Avoid trades, especially of minor pieces: every trade brings closer the endgame where the pawn falls.
D'abord bloquer : un cavalier en d5, dev: Blockade first: a knight on d5, in front of the pawn, is the ideal piece (no pawn can chase it) and stops its advance.
Échange les pièces actives de l'adversai: Trade off your opponent's active pieces, especially the light-squared bishop eyeing your king.
Puis attaquer le pion : tours sur la col: Then attack the pawn: rooks on the d-file, knights on c6 and f5, bishop on f6 or b6 against d4.
Chaque finale est bonne pour toi : n'aie: Every endgame is good for you: don't be afraid to simplify.
Le camp « propriétaire » a d4 et e3, san: The “owner” has d4 and e3 with no c-pawn; the other side has c6 and d5 with no e-pawn (Queen's Gambit Declined, Exchange Variation). Each side has its wing: the minority attack on the queenside for one, play on the kingside and the e-file for the other.
L'attaque de minorité : poussée b4-b5 (s: The minority attack: push b4-b5 (backed by a4 and Rb1) to trade on c6 and leave your opponent a weak c-pawn, isolated or backward, on a half-open file.
Autre plan : f3 puis e3-e4 pour gagner l: Other plan: f3 then e3-e4 to take the centre (knight on e2 rather than f3).
Cavalier vers e5 ou c5 une fois l'aile d: Knight to e5 or c5 once the queenside is open; rooks on the b- and c-files.
Ton jeu est à l'aile roi et sur la colon: Your play is on the kingside and the e-file: knight on e4, rook on e8 then sometimes e6-h6, bishop on d6 aiming at h2.
Contre l'attaque de minorité : …a5 pour: Against the minority attack: …a5 to slow it down, or, when b5 comes, a recapture or a …c5 push that doesn't leave you a weak c-pawn.
Garde ton fou de cases blanches actif (f: Keep your light-squared bishop active (f5, g4): it's the good bishop in this structure.
Un camp a un pion en d5 et la majorité c: One side has a pawn on d5 and the central majority; the other has c5 and d6, no e-pawn, and the queenside majority. Unbalanced positions: each side pushes its majority.
Ta majorité centrale : prépare e4-e5 (av: Your central majority: prepare e4-e5 (with f4 and Re1) to open the game and create a passed d-pawn.
Freine …b5 par a4 : sans cette poussée,: Stop …b5 with a4: without that push, your opponent lacks play.
Cavalier en c4 contre d6, le pion faible: Knight on c4 against d6, your opponent's weak pawn.
Ta majorité à l'aile dame : …a6, …Tb8 et: Your queenside majority: …a6, …Rb8 and …b5, then sometimes …c4, to get active pieces.
Le fou en g7 est ta meilleure pièce : ga: The bishop on g7 is your best piece: keep the long diagonal open.
Surveille e5 : ne laisse jamais passer e: Watch e5: never allow e4-e5 unless you're ready for it; a knight on e5 suits you.
Chaînes d4-e5 contre d5-e6 (française, C: Chains d4-e5 versus d5-e6 (French, Caro-Kann Advance). The chain points to the kingside: the side with e5 has space there; the other attacks the base of the chain.
Soutiens la chaîne : c3, Cf3, parfois f4: Support the chain: c3, Nf3, sometimes f4. If d4 falls, e5 falls next.
Ton jeu est à l'aile roi, du côté où poi: Your play is on the kingside, where the chain points: Bd3, Qg4, h4-h5, or f4-f5.
Le fou de cases blanches adverse est enf: Your opponent's light-squared bishop is locked behind e6: don't trade your good bishop for it.
Attaque la base de la chaîne : …c5 contr: Attack the base of the chain: …c5 against d4, with …Nc6, …Qb6 and a knight on f5, all hitting d4.
Puis …f6 contre e5 : la colonne f s'ouvr: Then …f6 against e5: the f-file opens for your rooks.
Ton fou de cases blanches est le mauvais: Your light-squared bishop is the bad bishop of this structure: trade it (…b6 and …Ba6) or get it out before …e6.
Chaînes d5-e4 contre d6-e5 (Est-indienne: Chains d5-e4 versus d6-e5 (closed King's Indian, Old Indian). Each chain points to a wing: you play on the side it points to. A race of attacks: every tempo counts.
Ta chaîne pointe vers l'aile dame : c4-c: Your chain points to the queenside: c4-c5 (prepared by b4, Nd2, Rc1) to open the c-file and attack d6 and c7.
Si l'adversaire joue …f5, f3 garde e4 so: If your opponent plays …f5, f3 keeps e4 solid; don't let their pawns reach your king without counterplay.
Échange son fou de cases noires si possi: Trade their dark-squared bishop if you can: it's their best defender.
Ta chaîne pointe vers l'aile roi : …f5,: Your chain points to the kingside: …f5, then …f4, …g5-g4 against the enemy king.
Cavaliers vers f6, g6, h4 ; tour en f7 p: Knights to f6, g6, h4; rook on f7 to defend c7 and use the f-file.
Ne perds pas de temps à l'aile dame : la: Don't waste time on the queenside: the race is won by a single tempo.
Pions c4 et e4 sans pion d, contre d6 sa: Pawns on c4 and e4 with no d-pawn, against d6 with no c-pawn (Sicilians, Accelerated Dragon, Hedgehog). The bind rules out your opponent's two freeing breaks, …b5 and …d5.
Garde l'étau : Fe3, Dd2, Tac1, Tfd1, par: Keep the bind: Be3, Qd2, Rac1, Rfd1, sometimes f3; as long as …b5 and …d5 are impossible, your opponent is short of space.
Un cavalier en d5 est très fort ; b3 et: A knight on d5 is very strong; b3 and a4 against …b5.
N'ouvre pas le jeu trop tôt : ton avanta: Don't open the game too early: your edge is space, and it grows with time.
Patience : structure hérisson (…a6, …b6,: Patience: Hedgehog setup (…a6, …b6, …e6, …Bb7) or bishop on g7, pieces on the back two ranks.
Échange des pièces (…Cxd4) pour libérer: Trade pieces (…Nxd4) to free up space.
Les ruptures …b5 et …d5 libèrent ta posi: The …b5 and …d5 breaks free your position: prepare them and play them when they work tactically.
Après d4 et …cxd4 : e4 sans pion d, cont: After d4 and …cxd4: e4 with no d-pawn, against d6 (or d7) with no c-pawn. Each side has a half-open file (d versus c); one has more space, the other a central majority. Opposite-side castling is common.
Contrôle d5 : Cc3-d5, Fg5 pour échanger: Control d5: Nc3-d5, Bg5 to trade the f6 knight that guards d5, Bc4 or Bb3.
Attaque à l'aile roi selon les pièces :: Attack on the kingside depending on the pieces: f4-f5, g4-g5; with opposite-side castling, speed decides.
Tour en d1 contre d6, souvent le pion fa: Rook on d1 against d6, often the weak pawn.
Ta colonne c : Tc8, cavalier vers c4, le: Your c-file: Rc8, knight to c4; the exchange sacrifice …Rxc3 is a classic theme.
La poussée …d5 libère ta position : quan: The …d5 break frees your position: when you can play it without losing material, you have usually equalised.
…b5-b4 chasse le cavalier c3 qui défend: …b5-b4 chases the c3 knight that guards e4 and d5. Careful with …e5: it leaves a hole on d5.
Pions d4, e3 et f4 (souvent c3) : un mur: Pawns on d4, e3 and f4 (often c3): a wall that holds e5 but leaves a hole on e4. The dark-squared bishop is locked behind the pawns.
Cavalier en e5, soutenu par d4 et f4 : c: Knight on e5, backed by d4 and f4: that's the heart of the plan.
Attaque à l'aile roi : Tf3-h3, Dh5 ou De: Kingside attack: Rf3-h3, Qh5 or Qe1-h4, sometimes g4-g5.
Ton fou de cases noires est mauvais : éc: Your dark-squared bishop is bad: trade it (b3 and Ba3) or accept playing without it; keep the light-squared bishop.
La case e4 est un trou : un cavalier y e: The e4 square is a hole: a knight there is very strong.
Échange le cavalier e5 (…Cd7) et le fou: Trade the e5 knight (…Nd7) and your opponent's light-squared bishop, their attacker.
Ruptures …c5 contre d4 et …f6 contre le: Breaks: …c5 against d4 and …f6 against the e5 knight.
Pions c3, d4 et e3 contre un pion d5 (Lo: Pawns on c3, d4 and e3 against a pawn on d5 (London, Colle, Slav). A very solid structure, but passive if it never moves: you need a break.
Sors ton fou de cases noires (Ff4 ou Fg5: Develop your dark-squared bishop (Bf4 or Bg5) before e3: afterwards it would be locked in.
Plan d'attaque : Ce5 et f4, puis l'aile: Attacking plan: Ne5 and f4, then the kingside (Rf3, Qh5).
Ou rupture e3-e4 (préparée par Cbd2, Dc2: Or the e3-e4 break (prepared by Nbd2, Qc2, Bd3) to open the centre at the right moment.
…c5 et …Db6 contre b2, affaibli par la s: …c5 and …Qb6 against b2, weakened once the dark-squared bishop has left.
Ou la rupture centrale …e5, préparée par: Or the central break …e5, prepared by …Nbd7 and …Qc7: it frees your game.
Pions e4-d3 contre e5-d6 (partie italien: Pawns e4-d3 against e5-d6 (slow Italian, closed Ruy Lopez). A closed, flexible structure: manoeuvring matters more than tactics, until the break.
La manœuvre de cavalier Cb1-d2-f1-g3 (ou: The knight manoeuvre Nb1-d2-f1-g3 (or …Nb8-d7-f8-g6) brings it to the kingside, towards f5 or h5.
La poussée d3-d4, préparée par c3, Te1 e: The d3-d4 push, prepared by c3, Re1 and h3, takes the centre: it's the main break.
a4 gagne de l'espace et freine …b5 ; h3: a4 gains space and stops …b5; h3 prevents the …Bg4 pin.
Rupture d'attaque : f2-f4 (ou …f5), une: Attacking break: f2-f4 (or …f5), once the knight has left f3 (or f6).
Pions e4 contre e5, plus de pions en d (: Pawns on e4 against e5, no more d-pawns (Scotch, Ruy Lopez Exchange, Philidor…). The d-file is open, and d5 and d4 are outposts.
La colonne d : la première tour qui s'y: The d-file: the first rook to settle there, with support, takes the initiative; doubling rooks is common.
Les cases d5 (pour les Blancs) et d4 (po: The d5 square (for White) and d4 (for Black) are ideal for a knight: c3 or …c6 takes them away from the opponent.
La poussée f4 (ou …f5) attaque le pion e: The f4 push (or …f5) attacks your opponent's e-pawn.
Les dames s'échangent souvent : pense dé: Queens often come off: start thinking about the endgame and your pawn majorities.
Pions d4 contre d5, plus de pions en e (: Pawns on d4 against d5, no more e-pawns (French Exchange, Petrov…). A symmetrical position: whoever creates the first weakness in the other camp takes the edge.
La colonne e est la lutte principale : T: The e-file is the main battleground: Re1, Re8, often doubled; the e5 (or e4) square for a knight.
Un fou contre un cavalier, un pion c ava: Bishop versus knight, an advanced c-pawn, a pin on g5: in a symmetrical position, these small pluses decide.
Les ruptures c4 (ou …c5) transforment la: The c4 (or …c5) breaks turn the structure into an isolated pawn: play them knowing which structure you'll get.
Plus aucun pion en d ni en e : les pièce: No pawns left on the d- or e-file: pieces rule. Development, the bishop pair and open files matter more than anything.
Les tours sur les colonnes d et e ; la p: Rooks on the d- and e-files; the first to control an open file, with support, takes the initiative.
Cavaliers au centre (d5, e5, d4, e4) qua: Knights in the centre (d5, e5, d4, e4) when no pawn can chase them; the bishop pair is a real asset.

Place ta dame à un saut de cavalier du r: Put your queen a knight's jump away from the enemy king and follow it that way: its space shrinks every move. Once the king is on the edge, bring your king over, then mate. Beware of stalemate: always leave it a square until the mate is ready.
La tour enferme le roi adverse derrière: The rook confines the enemy king behind a rank or a file. Your king faces theirs (opposition) and the rook gives check: the king steps back one line. If the kings aren't facing each other, make a waiting move with the rook, far from the enemy king.
Le roi devant son pion: King in front of its pawn
Ne pousse pas le pion tout de suite : av: Don't push the pawn right away: first bring your king in front of it, as far up as possible. King on the 6th rank in front of its pawn wins. Keep pawn moves in reserve to regain the opposition at the right moment.
Reste devant le pion. Quand le roi blanc: Stay in front of the pawn. When the white king comes closer, put your king facing it with one square in between (the opposition). Always step straight back towards the promotion square, never to the side: you can retake the opposition, and the final push will be stalemate.
Trois pions contre trois, rois loin : sa: Three pawns against three, kings far away: sacrifice the middle pawn. b6! If axb6, c6!; if cxb6, a6! One pawn gets through and queens before the black king arrives.
Ton roi est enfermé devant son pion. D'a: Your king is stuck in front of its pawn. First a check to push the black king further away (Rd1+), then the rook to the 4th rank (Rd4): when your king steps out, it will block the black rook's checks. That's the “bridge”.
Garde ta tour sur ta 3e rangée (ici la 6: Keep your rook on your 3rd rank (here the 6th) as long as the pawn hasn't reached it: the white king can't advance. As soon as the pawn reaches that rank, your rook drops all the way down and checks from behind: the white king has no shelter left.
Rapproche ta dame par des échecs et des: Bring your queen closer with checks and pins until the enemy king is forced in front of its pawn (on d1): it blocks its own promotion, and you gain a tempo to bring your king closer. Repeat until you win the pawn.
Pion de tour, et le fou blanc ne contrôl: Rook pawn, and the white bishop doesn't control the promotion square (h8 is dark): your king just has to hold the corner. Shuttle between h8, g8 and h7 without wandering off: the pawn can never queen.
